# The main purpose of enabling Meta’s Aggregated Event Measurement (AEM) is to gain more comprehensive insights into our iOS app campaigns. This is crucial because currently, a significant amount of valuable data for campaign optimization is lost due to Apple’s ATT (App Tracking Transparency) framework.

*Advanced data sharing* allows us to transmit all conversion events to Meta ads and attribute app installs and in-app events, regardless of a user's ATT consent status:

*Without Advanced data sharing*: Conversion event data is limited to users who have given consent through the ATT prompt. Events from non-consenting users are not shared or attributed.

*With Advanced data sharing enabled*: Conversion events can be shared for all users, irrespective of their ATT consent status. AppsFlyer attributes these events, and the shared data may include device-related information that does not rely on the device ID.

*Example for Bolt*: With this setup, we can optimize our iOS App ads more effectively because we have access to a larger set of data that was previously unavailable. Currently, this data limitation impacts our ability to refine and improve campaign performance, as most data from non-consenting users is lost. Advanced data sharing mitigates this loss and enhances campaign optimization efforts.


# For both web and app. Ideally we’d like to implement it to all verticals, or at least for Riders, Drivers and Delivery

# Data, including IP addresses and the IDFV is first collected by *Rudderstack*. Rudderstack acts as a data pipeline, collecting event data and sending it to various downstream tools. Rudderstack forwards the collected data to *Appsflyer*, which serves as an attribution and analytics platform. Appsflyer processes this data to track and attribute user interactions related to app installs and in-app events.  Once the data is processed in *Appsflyer*, Appsflyer transfers this data to *Meta*. This transfer allows Meta to leverage the data for enhanced ad targeting, campaign performance tracking, and optimization.

*Process between Meta and Appsflyer as stated in Appsflyers documentation*

Attribution flow:

Meta Ads appends attribution data to the deep link along with the AEM {{campaign_ids}} identifier. AppsFlyer receives the identifier with data showing on the deep link, then:

* Sends aggregate reporting data back to Meta ads
* Performs attribution based on the deep link information appended by Meta ads
* Includes attribution data from the deep link in raw data and aggregated data reports

{code:sql}-- time to recover 

SELECT 
CASE
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up = 0 THEN '00.) within 1 min'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up <= 1 THEN '01.) within 2 min'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up <= 2 THEN '02.) within 3 min'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 10 THEN '03.) within 10 min'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 30 THEN '04.) within 30 min'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 60 THEN '05.) within 1 hr'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 360 THEN '06.) within 6 hr'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 720 THEN '07.) within 12 hr'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 1440 THEN '08.) within 1 day'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 1440*7 THEN '09.) within 7 days'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 1440*14 THEN '10.) within 14 days'
	WHEN y.minutes_to_top_up < 1440*30 THEN '11.) within 30 days'
	ELSE '12.) after 30 days'
END AS minutes_to_top_up,
SUM(y.count_topups) AS total_count_topups,
ROUND(SUM(y.count_topups) * 1.00 / SUM(SUM(y.count_topups)) OVER (), 2) AS count_ratio,
SUM(y.recovered_amount) AS total_recovered_amount,
ROUND(SUM(y.recovered_amount) * 1.00 / SUM(SUM(y.recovered_amount)) OVER (), 2) AS amount_ratio
FROM (
SELECT 
x.minutes_to_top_up,
APPROX_DISTINCT(x.topup_id,0.0041) AS count_topups,
ROUND(SUM(x.amount_eur),2) AS recovered_amount
FROM (
WITH rejected_users AS (
SELECT DISTINCT
a.id,
a.created AS rejection_date,
a.meta.user_id,
a.meta.payment_method_type,
'https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/calculations/user_order_request/' || CAST(a.id AS varchar) AS calculation,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.balance_info.bolt_credit.amount_in_local_currency') AS REAL)*-1 AS bolt_credit_local_currency,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.balance_info.bolt_credit.amount_in_eur') AS REAL)*-1 AS bolt_credit_eur,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.balance_info.amount.amount_in_eur') AS REAL)*-1 AS amount_in_eur,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.balance_info.shadow_credit.amount_in_eur') AS REAL)*-1 AS shadow_credit_eur,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.balance_info.total_sum_eur') AS REAL)*-1 AS total_sum_eur,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.balance_bookings_info.failed_bookings_amount') AS REAL) AS failed_bookings_amount_eur,
CAST(json_extract_scalar(a.input, '$.order.price_prediction_eur') AS REAL) AS price_prediction_eur
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request a
WHERE a.created_hour BETWEEN date '2024-10-01' AND date '2024-10-31'
AND a.decision.decision = 'reject_top_up'
),
first_topup_date AS (
SELECT  
t.user_id,
ru.rejection_date,
MIN(t.created) AS first_successful_topup_paying_debt_after_rejection
FROM ng_balance_user.balance_user_order_top_up t
LEFT JOIN archive_analytical.user_top_up_request d ON d.meta.order_id = t.id 
JOIN rejected_users ru ON t.user_id = ru.user_id AND t.created > ru.rejection_date 
LEFT JOIN ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(t.created) AND r.currency = t.currency
WHERE t.created_date >= date '2024-10-01' 
AND d.created_hour >= date '2024-10-01'
AND t.state = 'successful'
AND CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.payment.balance.amount_eur') AS REAL) < 0
AND t.amount/r.rate*1.05 >= COALESCE(ru.bolt_credit_eur,ru.failed_bookings_amount_eur)
GROUP BY 1,2
),
order_group AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
ru.user_id,
ru.rejection_date,
CASE WHEN COALESCE(DATE_DIFF('minute',lag(ru.rejection_date) OVER(PARTITION BY ru.user_id ORDER BY ru.rejection_date),ru.rejection_date),0) <= 30 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS new_order_group_flag
FROM rejected_users ru
),
order_clusters AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
o.user_id,
o.rejection_date,
SUM(new_order_group_flag) OVER (PARTITION BY o.user_id ORDER BY o.rejection_date) AS order_group
FROM order_group o
),
real_time_to_recover AS (
SELECT  
ru.user_id, 
t.id,
MAX(DATE_DIFF('minute',ru.rejection_date,ftd.first_successful_topup_paying_debt_after_rejection)) AS real_minutes_to_top_up
FROM rejected_users ru 
LEFT JOIN first_topup_date ftd ON ftd.user_id = ru.user_id AND ftd.rejection_date = ru.rejection_date 
LEFT JOIN ng_balance_user.balance_user_order_top_up t ON t.user_id = ftd.user_id AND t.created = ftd.first_successful_topup_paying_debt_after_rejection AND t.state = 'successful' AND t.created_date >= date '2024-10-01'
LEFT JOIN ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(t.created) AND r.currency = t.currency
GROUP BY 1,2
)
SELECT DISTINCT 
ru.id, 
ru.rejection_date,
ru.user_id,
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY ru.user_id, t.id ORDER BY ru.rejection_date) AS row_number_top_up,
CASE WHEN t.id = lag(t.id) OVER(PARTITION BY ru.user_id ORDER BY ru.rejection_date) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS duplicated_topup,
ru.payment_method_type AS debt_payment_method_type,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.order.payment_method_type') AS top_up_payment_method_type, 
ROUND(COALESCE(ru.bolt_credit_eur,ru.failed_bookings_amount_eur),2) AS debt_eur,
ru.price_prediction_eur,
t.id AS topup_id,
t.created AS topup_created,
ftd.first_successful_topup_paying_debt_after_rejection,
ROUND(t.amount/r.rate,2) AS amount_eur,
rtr.real_minutes_to_top_up AS minutes_to_top_up
FROM rejected_users ru 
LEFT JOIN first_topup_date ftd ON ftd.user_id = ru.user_id AND ftd.rejection_date = ru.rejection_date 
LEFT JOIN ng_balance_user.balance_user_order_top_up t ON t.user_id = ftd.user_id AND t.created = ftd.first_successful_topup_paying_debt_after_rejection AND t.state = 'successful' AND t.created_date >= date '2024-10-01'
LEFT JOIN archive_analytical.user_top_up_request d ON d.meta.order_id = t.id AND CAST(json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.additional.payment.balance.amount_eur') AS REAL) < 0 AND d.created_hour >= date '2024-10-01'
LEFT JOIN ng_public.vw_currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(t.created) AND r.currency = t.currency
LEFT JOIN order_clusters oc ON oc.user_id = ru.user_id AND oc.rejection_date = ru.rejection_date 
LEFT JOIN real_time_to_recover rtr ON rtr.user_id = ru.user_id AND t.id = rtr.id
) AS x 
WHERE x.minutes_to_top_up IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 
) AS y
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1{code}

** Existing users will be targeted and activated via lifecycle communication saying “_Take a ride by using the promo code XXX and win an exclusive weekend getaway for 2 this winter!_”
*** They can use a promo code when taking trips. Intention is to include a disclaimer saying “_By taking part in this sweepstake, applying the promo code allows Bolt to contact winners via email_”.
* Structured as a sweepstake. 2 qualified winners will be able to go to a spa in Zurich.

* Just before user signs up to the campaign, we may want to consider include appropriate disclaimer wording.
** Should say that Bolt will process user’s data in accordance with privacy notice.
*** e.g. “_Your personal data will be processed solely to select and notify winners as part of this campaign. For more details, see Bolt's privacy notice available at [link]”_
** However, if we have T&Cs in place, then we can instead just refer to those (see
* We should have T&Cs for this campaign:
** Basic consideration should be fairness and transparency. The participants must understand how and on what conditions the prizes are assigned. “Random” allocation is possible, but this has to be clearly explained.
*** We then also have a much clearer privacy section, and we do not have to rely on disclaimers and default privacy notices. 
*** We also do not have to rely on consent or other lawful bases to process personal data - we can just rely on the T&C conditions requiring processing of PD.

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. * Simply stated blocked drivers are *not* allowed to create a new account to drive again since there’s a reason that they are blocked; we want them to stay off the platform. They need to wait til they are unblocked to drive again.

* Blocked drivers *do have the right* to delete their account. You can follow the correct process for that: [🚗 Driver: I want to delete my account|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360010217173]. However, if they want to register again we can detect that their previous account is blocked, and we can deny their request. (Just an fyi, we don’t ‘reactivate’ accounts, but create new ones)

To me, it makes sense that blocked drivers cannot just delete their account and create a new one to drive again. So I don’t think any changes need to be made in the articles.

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *24 October 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights*

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt

*Marketing Consents Management feature for couriers  - launched*👍 

*Problem*
Until now, couriers had only one way to opt-out of marketing communications they receive from us - via unsubscribe links, with no central view of marketing communication types and consents and no possibility to manage their consents granularly. 

*Solution*
We introduced a granular marketing consents management feature for couriers. It allows couriers to manage their marketing consents directly from the Courier app. Couriers can separately configure consents for each type of marketing communications (Bolt Products, Promotions, Partner Offers) and for each communication channel (sms, email, push notification, whatsapp, voice calls, app inbox, app banners).

*Markets*

* Globally to all markets

*Minimum app versions*
UA.1.40 / UI.1.40

Please share any feedback/issues in the [#feature-courier-consents|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C079Q0267NG] slack channel.

*Design Doc:*

# Bolt Products - which includes cross-promotion of other Bolt`s services and offers, such as th invitation to become a Driver; Soft opt-in consent enabled.
# Partner Offers - which includes third-party offers; Hard opt-in consent required - disabled by default.

# contract with company A with TIN 123 is linked with business company profile A. 
# if the company A moves and has new address but still has TIN 123, it can stay linked with profile A
# if the company A is liquidated/ends contract with Bolt > profile A is deactivated in admin
# if the same owners from company A create a new company B with new TIN > new contract > profile B is created even if owners and employees (users) are exactly the same as company A

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *20 October 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History* 



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/pl-pl/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/pl-pl/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt

Draft function for channel selection: (used this spreadsheet also for testing):

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sAv_4VNgL7i3mXPhIrSuFHa2q3QCuLsI8ltJ1ZKL1Qc/edit?gid=0#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1sAv_4VNgL7i3mXPhIrSuFHa2q3QCuLsI8ltJ1ZKL1Qc/edit?gid=0#gid=0|smart-link] 



{noformat}def get_channels_for_modelling(p_df, train_start_date):

    cost_cols = [c for c in p_df.columns if c.startswith("cost")]
    cost_df = p_df[p_df["date_date"] > train_start_date][cost_cols] # Will need to delete filtering here

    selected_columns = []
    cost_df = cost_df.replace(0, 0.1) # To avoid division by 0

    # Channel is eligible to be used in the model if:
    # 1) It's spend has changed at least once
    # 2) This change is greater than 25% of the minimum spend AND the change is greater than 95 Eur (100 with a gap) - comparing to baseline spend
    # 3) We use rolling mean to ensure changes are continuous for some time

    for column in cost_df.columns:
        baseline_spend = cost_df[column].iloc[:20].mean()

        rolling_mean = cost_df[column].rolling(window=20).mean()

        spend_change_prct = abs(rolling_mean - baseline_spend) / baseline_spend
        spend_change_abs = abs(rolling_mean - baseline_spend)

        #By using rolling mean we ensure that these conditions hold at least for the period of selected window
        significant_changes = (spend_change_prct >= 0.25) & (spend_change_abs >= 95)

        if significant_changes.sum() >= 1:
            selected_columns.append(column)
    return selected_columns{noformat}

Dear Daniel,

We write in relation to the deletion of your old Bolt account on 5 October, as well as in relation to your data subject rights request that we received on 7 October 2024.

We sincerely apologise for the deletion of your old Bolt account, which was due to a human error in the implementation of our fraud detection and prevention processes. After a thorough investigation, it has been determined that, unfortunately, your previous account cannot be restored due to technical limitations. We are reviewing this incident and will ensure that the relevant employee(s) are educated accordingly so that this does not happen again. We attach a copy of your personal data from the old account that is currently processed by Bolt and/or which we were able to retrieve from your old account before it was removed from our systems, for your records. We also remain committed to assisting you in every way possible to ensure a smooth transition, and we can guide you through the registration process to create a new account.

Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties. Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies. We therefore attach a copy of your personal data to which you are entitled, namely the text and phone conversations regarding your old account.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Your sincerely,

*Bolt Privacy Team*

Initial plan was using Cloud Run to run sftpgo and have it behind some load balancer. We found out that wasn’t going to work since Cloud Run only supports HTTP services (probably since it can run at scale 0 and cold start to serve responses)

We did some reading and came up with a new plan - on GCE you can run a Compute Instance with a container-optimised image and specify which container it runs in the metadata.

The customers bank SEB might have issues locating the incremental authorization. 

The reservations the customer is seeing are related to incremental authorizations.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

There was a Slack thread raised about the same issue this week if you would like to find out more.

A 15-day advance notice for pricing changes is not explicitly required in the T&Cs for Drivers (only for T&C changes as set in clause 14.2). However, providing 15 days' advance notice for pricing changes is a good practice, given the sensitivity of the topic (we introduced it in EE). This requirement is indirectly supported by EU law (explained below). 

*Overall:* +while it might be tolerable not to notify drivers in advance about price changes, consumers (riders) should certainly be informed ahead of time+ and given full transparency. The risk of violating consumer rights in these cases is considerably higher.

+*_Drivers_*+

*  [+EU Regulation on platform-to-business (P2B)+|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A32019R1150] requires providing business users (drivers) with 15 days advance notice about any changes to the T&C. While prices are not directly regulated by the T&C, they can significantly impact the operations of business users on the platform. Therefore, it is advised to communicate any changes to prices with a 15-day advance notice.

* Failure to do so would render the changes invalid and could result in claims of P2B Regulation violation by consumer protection authorities.

+*_Consumers_*+

* to prevent misleading commercial practices, +consumers must be informed before purchasing the services about (i) the principles of price calculation; (ii) the discount percentage applied to their purchase.+ 
* If price increase or test affecting  consumers is not communicated it could be treated as unfair pricing resulting in:
** the Equal Opportunities Ombudsman claims that Bolt discriminated against consumers. Bolt would need to present how consumers were selected, what specific financial benefit / loss was incurred by each consumer etc. The monetary fine could be up to 500 EUR + reputational damage. 
** for misleading the consumers, the Consumer Rights Authority could impose a fine of up to 5,000 EUR, it could be lower if that different prices were applied for a short period (4-6 weeks) and consumers were informed of the specific price for the service before ordering and purchasing it. 
** for unfair commercial activities, the Consumer Rights Authority could impose a fine of up to 3 % of a company's annual income for the previous financial year but not exceeding EUR 100,000.

*Related to consent, something that I’ve omitted in the form, but is essential to highlight: for Rider, we have a dedicated type of consent called “consent_travelling” for push and email channels.* When creating an account, this type of consent is by default turned off, so users need to explicitly opt in to receive travel-related comms. So I think the questions would be:

* Can we rely on this existing hard opt-in consent to start targeting users with location-based comms or do we need something additional? Do we need to update existing T&Cs or is this already covered since the consent already exists and some users have already provided consent?
* Can we use the same type of consent for Rentals and Business comms as well?
* This existing travelling consent only covers push and email as channels. Do we need to add it for in-apps as well, or can we treat location-based in-apps similar to other in-apps, i.e. exempt from consents?
* Is there anything additional from legal point of view that we need to keep in mind/take care of before we start targeting users with this consent?

[Courier substitution went live in EU on 26/07/2024. |https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CQL1E137B/p1721994778020839]It is a possibility for a courier to delegate his work to another person (who is not a Bolt courier).This is to protect ourselves from reclassification and we want to know who and when works instead of our couriers, since we know they do share their account/phone with other people, but we didn’t have visibility of this.

*How does it work?*
We collect information about substitutions: who works instead of our courier and when. This data could be shared with authorities in any situation (for example a request from the Police).

*How does it work from a courier perspective?*
There are several steps:

* a courier contact Customer Support (CS)
* CS asks to provide certain information: who will be working as a courier (name, last name, date of birth, phone number, email, ID, ID's expiry date) and when (time slots)
* the courier provides the information
* after checking the information, CS confirms, that the substitute can work

*What requests CS can receive and how to handle them?*
There can be different types of requests

# Create a substitute
# CS requests data,
# CS validates data manually (minimum age requirement, the name matches the provided document, the document isn't expired)
# CS goes to [this page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-courier/courierSubstitutions] creates a substitute and adds time frames (if provided)

# Add time slots  for already existing substitute

* CS receives a request to [this page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-courier/courierSubstitutions], locates the substitute, opens it, and adds a new time slot

# Deactivate a substitute

* CS receives a request to [this page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/delivery-courier/courierSubstitutions], locates the substitute, opens it, and presses the button {{Deactivate}}

*How many couriers will use it?*
We don't expect many couriers to use it.  5-10 requests from a courier per month per market.

*Implementations  limitations*
Please keep in mind that this functionality was implemented as MVP. Our goal was to release it, collect statistics, and then make
a decision about further development and improvements.*FAQ*

* Does substitution work for any courier? No, a courier should not work for a fleet, also should have an active account. 
* What do we show in the courier APP when a substitute works instead of a courier? So far we display the courier info, not substitute's
* Do we somehow control who is working right now: a substitute or a courier? No, we don't. Right now we only collect information on what time frames a substitute should work
* How many substitutions can have a courier? We  don't have limitations here
* Can a substitute work in a different city (not the same as a courier)? No, substitute works in the same city as a courier



So far, this opportunity is not used often. As per Admin, there is only 2 substitutions and CS has received 15 tickets with the issue key I want to add or remove a substitute (want_to_substitute_the_order_courier)

Hey [~accountid:5b7beb46b8624857f09efff9] , getting back to you with the main points on what we can / cannot say publicly re CCTVs.

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*What we can say*
{panel}

* *General statements about our privacy mission / our compliance with laws*, such as "Bolt is committed to upholding the highest privacy standards for our customers and partners."
* *Roles and responsibilities of drivers<>Bolt when it comes to data processing under privacy laws*, such as "Drivers using CCTV cameras are considered independent data controllers under privacy regulations, meaning they bear responsibility for the lawful handling of any personal data collected."
* *Expectations regarding compliance with privacy laws*, such as "Drivers who choose to use CCTV cameras are expected to ensure their practices comply with local and EU privacy laws, specifically concerning data transparency, storage, and purpose for data use." or "Drivers  using CCTV cameras are accountable for adhering to privacy regulations and may face legal consequences in the event of non-compliance."
* *Recommendation (not instruction) to comply with transparency requirements under privacy laws,* such as "Drivers using CCTV are advised to display appropriate CCTV signage that clearly communicates the purpose of recording, data retention period, controller’s identity, and how customers can access a detailed privacy notice." and "We recommend that drivers make a Privacy Notice available, detailing how personal data from CCTV recordings is processed and where customers can access it if needed."
* *I also recommend adding a disclaimer somewhere in the page, explaining that this is guidance and not instructions,* such as: "While we offer guidance on privacy best practices, drivers have the discretion to determine their own policies as independent controllers, though they are still accountable under applicable laws."
* *I assume we want to protect our passengers against their data being published online, e.g. on Tiktok or Youtube, however, we can’t prohibit that. We can however advise against doing so:* 
** *Something like this about sharing data on social media*: "To maintain privacy and uphold legal standards, we discourage drivers from posting CCTV footage of customers on social media platforms without clear legal justification and an appropriate legal basis (such as consent)." 
** *Disclaimer that data sharing can be prohibited under laws and they must ensure legality:* "Drivers are encouraged to review privacy laws before sharing any CCTV footage. Unauthorized sharing of recordings can lead to privacy law violations and potential legal consequences." or "Drivers must ensure that any CCTV footage containing personal data is processed lawfully, fairly, and transparently, which potentially does not allow for public posting without a valid legal basis." or "Drivers are advised to keep CCTV footage strictly limited to necessary parties and to avoid any unnecessary disclosure that could breach data protection regulations."



{panel:bgColor=#ffebe6}
*What we cannot say*
{panel}

*Statements that would imply control over drivers' use of data:*

* Avoid saying, "We control or regulate the use of CCTV cameras by drivers or couriers."
* Avoid statements like, "Drivers are legally required to follow our specific guidelines on CCTV use."
* Avoid wording that implies control over drivers' independent decisions, such as, "We dictate how drivers must handle CCTV data."
* Avoid claims like, "We monitor or review all CCTV compliance practices for every driver.", or anything that might suggest that.

*Statements that would assume responsibility regarding transparency requirements:*

* Do not state, "We require all drivers with CCTV to submit Privacy Notices to us for approval."
* Avoid making guarantees, such as, "All drivers using CCTV fully comply with privacy laws."

*Statements that suggest our responsibility for data storage/security:*

* Avoid phrases like, "We take responsibility for any data breaches from drivers’ CCTV cameras" or “Bolt ensures the security of CCTV data”
* Do not suggest that customers can access CCTV footage or data directly through your platform, such as, "Customers can request their CCTV data directly from us."

*Statements related to data sharing publicly on social media or with 3rd parties:*

* Avoid saying, "We control whether or not drivers share CCTV recordings publicly."
* Do not state, "Drivers are strictly prohibited from sharing any CCTV footage publicly, and none of our drivers do so."
* Do not imply that obtaining customer consent automatically allows public sharing, such as, "If a driver gets consent, they can share footage on social media."
* Avoid stating, "Drivers are allowed to share footage publicly if they think it’s necessary."



[~accountid:5b7beb46b8624857f09efff9] , as you see from these points, they all serve the same goal - we can’t assume legal responsibility for drivers' actions re CCTV, we don’t have to control what they do. Most importantly - even if we post these anywhere publicly (e.g. on Blog) - *this doesn’t create a ground for us to take actions against drivers*, unless it is specifically prohibited and mentioned in the Terms and Conditions applicable in that specific market.

In other words - if driver uploads CCTV footage to Youtube, this page can’t be used as an instrument to block the driver. Any actions against drivers in these cases need to be validated by the legal team (not privacy team).

Happy to discuss if something’s unclear 🙂

I was first thinking that we would have two processes:

# selecting channels
# selecting the period

However, found out that very often these two processes would have circular dependency if done separately or sometimes they could get internally contradictory.

So I decided to build one process on the other one:

* We are choosing both the channels and the period based on variance in spend
* So it makes sense to identify some spots of “significant change“
* Select some maximal period that we want to use for data modelling (14 months for now)
* Be looking for a maximal period inside these 14 months with the earliest significant change.



Idea to think for the future - how do we feel about the models picking up more than one experiment? Do we just take only the most recent (=relevant) one or are we OK with one channel having multiple increases?

Would we want to find minimal period where each channel would have just one change?

*Argument against:*

* often the experiments happen at different levels of spend. Meaning that if we include more experiments, we have more understanding of the curve

_From an initial, overall perspective, it would be really helpful to understand what the objective of the card scheme is, i.e. what issues it is trying to solve for Bolt’s business customers. We had initially assumed that it would be about tracking employee expenses more accurately, but the ability to withdraw cash using the cards seems to run contrary to that. As part of that, it would also be helpful to understand where this is being driven from, e.g. is this an initiative from the Product team and is it primarily a European initiative with the UK just being included as part of that?_

*_Background and our understanding_*

* _We understand that Bolt is looking to introduce a “Bolt Card” programme. This will involve the issue of physical cards to business customers._
* _The cards would be pre-loaded with funds from the business customers, who would pass the money to Bolt, to load to the cards. We assume that the cards would then be reloadable by businesses paying further monies to Bolt._
* _The business customers will give these cards to their employees who will use them to make purchases of transport-related services from both Bolt and third-parties:_
** _insofar as concerns payments to Bolt, we assume the employees will input the card details into their payment information in the app, in the same way as they would input the details of their credit/debit cards;_
** _insofar as concerns payments to third-parties, we assume the cards can be used as a payment method in the same way as a normal debit card can be used._
* _The employees would also be able to physically withdraw cash from the cards through ATMs (we assume this results in the draw down of funds held in a Bolt account?)._
* _The card is intended to be used in the UK and overseas, resulting in Bolt charging foreign exchange fees._
* _The card spending would be limited to the amount pre-loaded onto the card. For example, if the card was pre-loaded with £100, it would not be possible for the customer to spend £110._
* _There would be no intention for the card to be structured such that Bolt buys and supplies on the services purchased using the cards, rather, the cards would simply be a method of the businesses themselves purchasing the services._
* _We understand Bolt is intending to make a service charge to the business customer. We understand it as a subscription / similar charge on a regular basis that allows business customers to obtain increased functionality of the Bolt app such as getting expense reports, encourages business customers to use one app for monitoring expenses through online reports and facilitates the pre-loading of the cards._

_Please let us know if our understanding above is not correct as it may affect our advice._

*_Points to clarify_*

# _Could you please provide us with a few more details concerning how the Bolt Card scheme would work overall? In particular:_
## _What is Bolt looking to achieve / solve for the business customer with the introduction of the new programme?_
## _Will Bolt collaborate with a bank or financial company to allow the card to be used (i) as a payment method vis-à-vis third-parties with whom there is not a separate contractual agreement with Bolt committing them to accept the card as a payment method; (ii) to withdraw funds from a bank account via ATMs (i.e. will the card be a white labelled arrangement)? If so:_
### _could you please provide further details on any discussions to date; and_
### _could you confirm the specific roles of Bolt and the other parties (e.g. the financial institution and any other party) in respect of the arrangements. For example, will there be a contract between the business customer and the bank, a separate contract between Bolt and the bank and a separate contract between Bolt and the business customer?_
## _If Bolt is not intending to collaborate with a bank or financial company, on what basis is it anticipated that third-parties will accept the card as a form of payment. For example, will Bolt have agreements with the relevant third-parties committing them to accept the cards as a form of payment?_

 

# _We understand Bolt is intending to make a service charge to the business customer. We understand it as a subscription / similar charge on a regular basis that allows business customers to obtain increased functionality of the Bolt app such as getting expense reports, encourages business customers to use one app for expenses and facilitates the pre-loading of the cards. Could you please confirm our understanding is correct?_

# _How would the pre-loading of cards work? In particular:_

* _What are the timings around the business customer sending the money to Bolt and Bolt uploading the money to the card?_
* _What happens if the customer spends less in a month than the pre-loaded amount, i.e. could the funds ever ‘expire’?_

 

# _We understand Bolt is only intending to recognise revenue income from the different charges outlined in the excel spreadsheet “Pricing & Fees-Bolt Business Cards” (i.e. not the pre-loaded amounts). Please confirm our understanding is correct?_

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 



Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *14 October 2024.*



After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.



We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *All Data*



For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/uk-ua/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.



*Your rights* 



In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 



If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.





Yours sincerely,



Bolt

CROSS JOIN UNNEST (d.decision.actions) AS a(actions)

*Right to Return without Purchase Obligation*

The contract allows Bolt to return vehicles to the leasing provider post-lease, with the vehicles’ condition meeting contractual standards (e.g., no excessive wear or damage beyond standard use)

Bolt, therefore, does not have an obligation to purchase the vehicles at lease end. The contract explicitly excludes any end-of-term purchase requirement for Bolt.

* *Section C.I.14(f)*: “Ein Erwerb des Fahrzeuges vom Leasing-Geber durch den Leasing-Nehmer nach Vertragsablauf *ist ausgeschlossen*.” 
(However, this limitation applies only to the relationship between the leasing provider (VW) and Bolt, meaning Bolt is not required to purchase vehicles at the end of the lease. This does not, in my view, prevent Jacobs Group (the Handelspartner) from purchasing the vehicles from VW and subsequently selling them to Bolt.)

*Condition Standards for Vehicle Return*

Returned vehicles must be in a condition consistent with age and mileage, allowing for normal wear and tear, but must still be safe and operational.

* *Section C.I.14(b)*: “Bei der Rückgabe muss das Fahrzeug in einem dem Alter und der vertragsgemäßen Fahrleistung entsprechenden Erhaltungszustand, frei von Schäden sowie verkehrs- und betriebssicher sein. Normale Verschleißspuren gelten nicht als Schaden.” 

*Liability for Excess Damage (Minderwert)*

If returned vehicles exceed normal wear and tear, Bolt is responsible for covering depreciation or repair costs. Disagreements on damage levels can be resolved through an independent expert, with both parties sharing the expert’s fee.

* *Section C.I.14(c)*: “Können sich die Vertragspartner über einen vom Leasing-Nehmer auszugleichenden Minderwert nicht einigen, wird der Minderwert auf Veranlassung des Leasing-Gebers mit Zustimmung des Leasing-Nehmers durch einen öffentlich bestellten und vereidigten Sachverständigen oder ein unabhängiges Sachverständigenunternehmen ermittelt. Die Kosten tragen die Vertragspartner je zur Hälfte.” 

So in relation to this contract and in relation to the leasing provider (VW) Bolt is not required to purchase the leasing vehicles. However, this is merely the relationship between the leasing provider (VW) and Bolt. This might change in case there is another contract between the Handelspartner (Jacobs Group).

Proposals:

* {{innodb_buffer_pool_size}}:
** min: 1GiB
** max overall: 1152 GiB (soft), 2048 GiB (hard)
** max per available RAM: 73% (hard)
** max per buffer pool instance (soft): 18 GiB (soft), 32 GiB (hard)
** default: 70% of available RAM
* {{innodb_buffer_pool_instances}}:
** min: 8
** max: 64
** for 16, 32, 48 or 64 CPU cores: same as CPU core count
** default: 8 (do not set)
* {{innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size}}:
** min: 128 MiB
** max: 2 GiB
** default: 128 MiB (do not set)

----

When creating a new instance:

# Get {{cpu_count}} and {{ram_gb}}
# Set {{innodb_buffer_pool_instances}}:
#* max of (8, {{cpu_count}})
#* no more than 64
# Set {{innodb_buffer_pool_size}}:
#* if {{ram_gb}} < 4 GiB: default (128 MiB)
#* else: min of
#** {{innodb_buffer_pool_instances}} * 18 GiB
#** {{ram_gb}} * 70%
#** no more than 1152 GiB
# Set {{innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size}}:
#* if {{innodb_buffer_pool_size}} > 1000 GiB: 2 GiB
#* else if {{innodb_buffer_pool_size}} > 500 GiB: 1 GiB
#* else if {{innodb_buffer_pool_size}} > 250 GiB: 512 MiB
#* else if {{innodb_buffer_pool_size}} > 125 GiB: 256 MiB
#* else: default (128 MiB)

----

Reasons:

* Known limits listed in the task description
* {{innodb_buffer_pool_instances}} and {{innodb_buffer_pool_chunk_size}} can be only be changed on MySQL restart while buffer size can be changed dynamically
* pool size 1152 GiB (soft max) – 64 instances x 18 GiB
* pool size 2048 GiB (hard max): 64 instances x 32 GiB

Hello Team,

We have received the following feedback from Zoom:

[~accountid:712020:548c71a6-d1f4-404d-9c5e-482bc0de371a] : _“With regard to the MSA - we are fine to remove the link to US law and simply reference the DPA. I attach the approved version.”_

[~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a] : “_With regard to the DPA - my request is that you accept the version previously provided. We reviewed your commentary - and sought to address the points below with detailed explanations. While I can understand some of the points, it is inherently challenging for us to make bespoke or operational changes to a document relied upon by hundreds of thousands of customers. This is the case however small and apparently innocuous the changes may appear - as they could have unintended consequences or create significant unforeseen internal costs (where they seek to create bespoke processes for an individual customer across our large customer base)._

*Commentary on DPA requests:*

# *Processor Obligations* *2.5* - Restating obligations as a processor could create confusion as this is already clearly set out in 2.2. Ultimately we are clearly a data processor, and our processing limitations are clearly stated. We would request our standard position is therefore accepted, as these changes do not appear to change our status. If customer is seeking to limit our processing beyond what is already stated in our DPA, then this could be problematic.
# *Data Flows* *7.5/7.6* - This provision provides a standard mechanism to operate at scale and manage data transfer compliance with laws - particularly should laws change - at scale. This is not something Zoom is minded to change unless genuinely required, and given customer's regular audit right, they would be able to review and ensure compliance. We would also note that in all cases, we are required to comply with laws.
# *Data Subject Requests 8* - Requesting a data subject response within 3 business days is quite inconsistent with the customer's timeline of 1 month. We would also remark that it is quite unlikely that Zoom would receive such a request as a user is far more likely to engage with the account holder directly. Accordingly, we would not implement a bespoke internal process for a very unlikely activity in this manner, and we would request that our standard position applies- which requires prompt notification in this unlikely event.
# *Audit* - Zoom spends considering financial resources in its own third party audits (including ISO27001 and SOC2). These are conducted to avoid customer having to conduct bespoke reports, except in extreme cases. For this reason, Zoom does not feel it is appropriate to share an additional customer specific audit cost - we feel the likelihood of customer requiring a bespoke audit beyond reviewing all of the third party attestations, reports, and other information generally provided, as unlikely. 
# *Bespoke details on security reporting* - Zoom has an industry standard approach which broadly aligns to the principles espoused. However, we would request that operational details are not buried in the body of our DPA. We will provide the details to the contact referenced in the DPA or on the account.
# *Indemnification/Liability* - Zoom does not offer these indemnities. We would request that you reflect on the fact that the data is encrypted and Zoom does not have visibility to the data. Zoom does not accordingly offer such indemnities. Moreover, given the level of control the customer has over its usage of the platform and the data being processed, it would not be appropriate to sweep away remoteness or duty to mitigate losses, as an indemnity seeks to do. Given this context, we would request that you reconsider, as such indemnifications are not constructs that Zoom provides, nor are they considered reasonable given the context above. “

Could you please share your thoughts on this and how you think we should proceed? I’d be happy to provide any support needed.

Thanks,

Polina

The main issue found: added size originated from the desugaring library, which adds even more Java 9 compatible classes into the final classpath. Especially almost the whole {{java.util}} package was added, which resulted in two more dex files being added. 

For a moment, we cannot do anything with this, as the disabling desugaring stage requires us to disable it through the whole chain of dependencies (which are comms chat SDK, for instance) + rewriting the parts of the rider code in the way it would use backward compatible language constructions.

Also, for some reason, one of Google’s libraries added the junit runtime classes: no way to check in advance if it was added by mistake if the runtime code relies on it, so we keep it as is until Google finds this issue by themselves or someone reports it to them.

Thanks for bringing this up! We used to have market-specific articles but switched to a single general one. This is because cancellation fee thresholds can vary not just by country, but also by city or ride category. Local OPS can also change these settings, so our articles become outdated or incomplete quickly. 

Both riders and drivers receive a direct indication in their app when a threshold is reached, whether for a free cancellation timeframe or waiting at the pickup.

Agents can check the cancellation fee setup by opening the Order page, selecting _Open in JSON_ at the bottom of the left panel, and going to the _Pricing_ tab. From there, you'll see the following details:

* {{cancellation_fee}} - The amount charged as a cancellation fee in local currency.
* {{cancel_without_fee_seconds}} - The free cancellation timeframe in seconds.
* {{client_did_not_show_after_seconds}} - After this period, the driver can cancel the ride and will be eligible for the cancellation fee.

The shortened guide is in our article 🚗[ Driver: I didn't receive a cancellation fee|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360013304500?country=global&language=en]. I’ll go ahead and close this case now. Thank you for your understanding.

h1. CCT - Simplified tester 

A simplified version of the Cobra Controller Tester is needed to understand the quantity of falsely diagnosed controllers, before investing more resources into building an automated tester.

h2. Tester description

A simplified version of the Cobra Controller Tester consists of two parts: Cobra iron bird and scooter for test rides. This way all controller functionality will be tested. 

!image-20241111-113904.png|width=1216,height=1003,alt="image-20241111-113904.png"!

*Picture 1.* CCT iron bird block diagram

Cobra iron bird will be used to test following features:

# Controller current consumption
# RS485 communication
# Errors 
# Lights
# Battery lock
# Throttle 
# Brakes
# Backup battery

Test ride will be used to test the rest of the functions. 

# Motor under load 
# Communication with battery
# ID pin

h2. Software requirements

Iron bird is controlled with a PC. The main functionality of the PC is to control the PSU, communicate with the controller, and request user input. The test program needs to include a graphical user interface (GUI) for a better operator experience and easier understanding. 

Controlling the PSU is done over a serial-USB (COM) interface. Communication with the controller is done using a USB-RS485 converter. Communication involves reading and writing values to different controller addresses and verifying that values are correct. The tester primarily relies on user input, such as applying throttle or brakes or checking if lights are turned on. Most of the test steps are used in protocol tester, which could make the software development easier.

An important part of the tester is saving test steps, values and results for future reference.

Test sequence can be found here: [https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eHC4R8cMQQQ-2pDlgwSpSBJGPfHXjFtw/edit?gid=157046051#gid=157046051|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1eHC4R8cMQQQ-2pDlgwSpSBJGPfHXjFtw/edit?gid=157046051#gid=157046051|smart-link]

# *Retrieval Order Differences*: As TiDB is a distributed DBMS, the retrieval order may differ depending on the number of TiKV nodes, unless an explicit {{ORDER BY}} statement is used.
# *DBD::mysql driver*:  The reason the data appears different is due to how the {{pt-upgrade}} tool interacts databases with Perl’s {{DBD::mysql}} driver, which MySQL and TiDB handle differently. For instance, if you use {{mysqlcli}} to retrieve the same data, no difference will be observed.

Thank you for escalating to Customer Payments team. The customers don't always have a great visibility when the pre-authorization has been returned to them. Returning the pre-authorization is not something Bolt has much control over. 
Depending on the bank the pre-authorization charges can take up to a month to be returned to the customer. 
If the Authorization state is Captured then everything is fine on our side and the customer has to check with their bank. 

Please only escalate the issue to Payment Operations team if

1. The funds have not been returned after 30 days and customer has checked with their bank

2. The state has been stuck in authorization for more than 24 hours. (72h for Micro Mobility) 

3. The state of the authorization is failed or error. 

Please leave a comment on the ticket if you still want it to be escalated to the Customer Payments team. Else the ticket will be closed in 5 days.

# _Could you please provide us with a few more details concerning how the Bolt Card scheme would work overall? In particular:_
## _What is Bolt looking to achieve / solve for the business customer with the introduction of the new programme?_
#*Bolt today has an expense management software for Bolt Business Customers but is only able to capture transactions that happen within the Bolt Ecosystem (Rides, Food). By introducing a card as global payment instrument, Bolt will be able to use the expense management software more expansively.*
## _Will Bolt collaborate with a bank or financial company to allow the card to be used (i) as a payment method vis-à-vis third-parties with whom there is not a separate contractual agreement with Bolt committing them to accept the card as a payment method; (ii) to withdraw funds from a bank account via ATMs (i.e. will the card be a white labelled arrangement)? If so:_
### _could you please provide further details on any discussions to date; and_
#### *Bolt will contract with a software company that will manage the service for them; the software company will be orchestrating contracts with card issuing bank, card issuing bank and kyc companies to setup the card program for Bolt.* 
#### *The card issuing will be white-labelled but will belong to issuer bank. The ATM can be used to withdraw funds already added by Bolt Business customer.*
### _could you confirm the specific roles of Bolt and the other parties (e.g. the financial institution and any other party) in respect of the arrangements. #### *Bolt Business customer, at onboarding, will enter the contract with Bolt & the issuer bank by accepting independent terms and conditions for both. The Bolt business customer will then undergo KYC process. In case Bolt Business customer decided to assign card to their employee, their employee will also accept cardholder terms & conditions separately but not have to undergo KYC.*
## _If Bolt is not intending to collaborate with a bank or financial company, on what basis is it anticipated that third-parties will accept the card as a form of payment. # _Could you please clarify how the ATM withdrawals would work? We understand this would be from the money already pre-loaded on the cards and not subject to a maximum credit amount. Please confirm our understanding is correct._

*Card transactions can be disputed by the cardholder incase of fraud. If they are disputed, there is a process that will take place to recover the amount from the acquiring bank. {quote}Update on the NA FOTA problem. What have I tested so far:

# Updated the modem fw to the latest version. Didn't changed anything.
# Tried pure socket test on TCP/IP level without MQTT or any FOTA business logic. This also fails in a similar way
# Tried tuning TCP/IP buffer sizes inside esp lwip stack. Didn't have any effect.
# Throttling on the server side makes things better but doesn't resolve the problem.
# Contacted Quectel support. No helpful information from their side so far.
# Tried analyzing PPP/TCP frames. I can see that when the connection 'freezes' the IOT starts receiving TCP frames with the same acknowledgement number over and over. These frames are acked by the TCP/IP stack and sent to the modem. But for some reason these acknowledgements do not reach the server. Eventually the server terminates the connection due to timeout. Also found this topic [https://forums.quectel.com/t/eg-915q-issue-using-ppp-with-tcp/24097|https://forums.quectel.com/t/eg-915q-issue-using-ppp-with-tcp/24097|smart-link]  on Quectel forum which describes the same problem with EG915Q. This kind of hints that possibly there is a problem with EG915Q PPP server.

What can be done imo?

# In order for Quectel support to be able to help modem logs have to be collected. As the logs are collected using Quectel proprietary tools the problem has to be repeated with the modem connected to Windows machine somewhere in US.
# Test with different pin compatible modem which supports EU and US frequencies. EG916 for example, I have briefly checked that EG91 series should be pin compatible.
# We could try using AT commands (or maybe even transparent mode) instead of PPP. This would require significant effort on fw side to support the new driver. But in theory we could continue using the same MQTT library so the rest of system the network interface would be the same. Connection speed when using AT commands would definitely be smaller (sub 1Mbit). If we stick to this solution this would mean that in future we would have to support two types of modem drivers which is obviously not good.{quote}

The simple option: every time we add or remove cities from a group, we actually make a new group with a new list of participating cities. The downside: there’s no connection between the old and the new version of the city group. If we want city groups to be entities of their own, meaning, we know there’s a specific group and how the specific group has changed over time, we need to have a better structure.

There’s a number of ways one can achieve this. From analytics perspective we need something like this. 

# A slowly changing dimension for city group
# All fact tables refer to the version of the city group that was relevant at the time of the fact

||*city_group_history_id*||*city_group_id*||*valid_from*||*valid_to*||*city_id_list*||
|1|1|2024-01-01 00:00|2024-01-10 23:59|1,2,3|
|2|1|2024-01-11 00:00| |1,2|
|3|2|2024-01-21 00:00|2024-01-25 23:59|4,5|
|4|2|2024-01-26 00:00|2024-01-31 23:59|4,5,6|
|5|3|2024-01-01 00:00| |7,8|

||*event_id*||*event_name*||*event_ts*||*city_group_history_id*||*city_group_id (found from city group table based on city_group_history_id, not necessarily stored in the fact table)*||
|1|campaign_created|2024-01-01 10:00|1|1|
|2|campaign_updated|2024-01-11 10:00|2|1|

In practice, you might store the data differently in the application backend, but from analytics perspective it must be possible to turn the data into a similar format that I described. 

There’s probably also a separate table to provide us with city group attributes:

||*city_group_id*||*city_group_name*||
|1|Estonia small towns|
|2|Germany medium towns for supply bonuses|

If you want, you can add versioning on top of this as well. Then you have a choice: either you keep one versioning table for all the attributes (if any attribute changes, there will be a new version of the entity) or you keep separate versioning tables (one for name changes, one for … etc). 

[https://digikogu.taltech.ee/et/item/c9c305c7-c851-4884-909d-ab9748b8e560|https://digikogu.taltech.ee/et/item/c9c305c7-c851-4884-909d-ab9748b8e560|smart-link]  - read this if you want to understand the whole complexity 🙂

Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount. 


Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,
Marten

Mihkel Klementsov opened some drum brakes and found one interesting thing - the lower springs were all deformed (the ones that are close to the butterfly)



Based on those pictures I suspect that the spring has been too short because the preload has already deformed it a lot. That big deformation might cause a spring cracking.

The second theory is that the spring might be too strong and a little too short. In this case, if the spring is too short, we would have to stretch the spring more than necessary, and if the material is too strong, we would already have overstretched the spring at its initial position. Later, during braking, the spring would stretch even more, and we would exceed the stress limit, causing the spring to break.

A/B test ended. [Here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AIAwmcp3NX4n4ylFptDKm3VtjLi9MfONGEpF63qir-M/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.tsjsz18ky8kz] is an analysis of the experiment. All in all, the feature is useful in reducing courier time and CS tickets.

[https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07D55FP0JU/p1731411532977969|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C07D55FP0JU/p1731411532977969|smart-link] 

Key points:

* The courier arrival notification is associated with a decline in the time from courier arrival to order delivered (hereafter called arrival-delivery time simply for brevity’s sake) by an average of 3.47 seconds (2.5%) per order. This is evaluated as a cost saving of approx 328K EUR per year. *There is also a decline in eater-initiated CS cases by 4% for the reason “order not delivered”. This is worth roughly 14.5K EUR in potentially saved CS costs. As a result, the feature is worth roughly 342.5K EUR per year in saved costs.*
* In terms of feature effectiveness, we note that the arrival-delivery courier time experiences a decline for all orders placed outside of late night to early morning hours (12-6AM, roughly). We only observe a decline occurring for existing users, and not new users.
* The difference in arrival-delivery courier time is greatest for users who are *somewhat frequent  (1-9 orders in the past 2 months)*, but not the top-most frequent customers. The difference is also greater for users who make orders to their *non-primary addresses* (addresses which are not the most common for a given user).
* Three groups of (non-mutually exclusive) users do not benefit from the feature, with very different characteristics:
** New/infrequent users do not benefit, even though they have a large opportunity scope to do so. Despite receiving notifications, their arrival-delivery courier time does not reduce - especially those with little-to-no engagement with the active order screen
** The top most frequent users do not benefit, but they unlikely have much scope to benefit. They experience the lowest arrival-delivery courier time as it is; they are likely familiar with the flows and are prepared to accept deliveries.
** Users with orders placed at night (12-6AM) do not appear to benefit from notifications, despite having the opportunity scope to do so
* The difference appears to be greater for users who exhibit little-to-no engagement of the active order screen. Users who engage with the screen are more likely to be aware of the order status and not benefit much from additional notifications. However, here we see a divergence between new and existing users:
** Existing users with the least engagement with the active order screen benefit the most from the feature

New users with the least engagement with the active order exhibit the largest _uptick_ in average arrival-delivery courier time (directionally, insignificant due to small samples)

The mediation for this matter took place today via telephone, see summary below: 



*Date:* 12 November 2024 

*Present:* Anusha Balachandre and Mediator 

*Mediation Summary:*

* *Opening statement from mediator:* The mediator encouraged both parties to actively seek a resolution to avoid court proceedings, noting that any settlement reached would be legally binding.
* *Authority to Settle*: AB confirmed her authority to settle on behalf of Bolt Services UK Limited.
* *Driver’s Claim:* The driver asserted that he drives in the executive category and was unable to drive on a busy Friday and Saturday night, resulting in a loss of earnings due to the passenger vomiting in the car. The driver said that his car was wet and smelt so he was not able to use this on Friday and Saturday. The driver feels that Bolt failed to provide sufficient support, and despite a cleaning fee payment of £60 from Bolt, they seek additional compensation, including £300 for loss of earnings, £140 for stress, £50 for the application court fee and £60 for the cleaning fee (a total of £550). 
* *Bolt’s Position:* AB emphasised that Bolt’s terms and conditions, specify that Bolt is not liable for loss of earnings. AB questioned the £550 claimed by the driver, seeking a detailed breakdown of the schedule of loss, AB asked why the £60 cleaning fee has been included in the scheduled of loss (especially given that the driver has acknowledged in the claim form that this has been paid out by Bolt). AB also mentioned that if the driver is making a claim for stress/distress this would be a personal injury claim (this claim has not been made out), therefore AB asked the mediator to seek clarity in the £140 compensation request. 
*  The mediator asked if Bolt would be willing to pay for these loss of earnings as the mediator mentioned that the driver was unable to drive on Friday and Saturday, AB reiterated that Bolt would not exceed its existing offer of £50.
* *Mediator’s Response:* The mediator conveyed that the driver seeks compensation due to lack of support from Bolt as the driver wanted Bolt to collect the compensation from the passenger. The driver is  willing to remove the £60 cleaning fee from the schedule of loss but is unwilling to accept less than £350 as the driver believes that this reflects the potential earnings missed over the weekend.
* *Conclusion:* Mediation ended without a resolution. 
* *Next Steps*: The mediator advised the parties to continue discussions independently, with the option to settle before the court hearing, the hearing will not be allocated to the court for 7-9months due to the courts backlog. 

+*Summary*+

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *10 October 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

Dear José*,* 

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *11 October 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/pt-pt/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/pt-pt/privacy/|smart-link] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

* The AirFlow DAG starts and executes the collection of the data using a Spark job and stores results in S3
* The periodicity job execution can be adjusted to Client needs (MaestroQA polls the S3 bucket for new data every hour)

Hi Klára,

I will try to give you a short explanation about how everything works.

We have *dispatch areas* in our system which are special defined areas (in admin-panel, usually these are airports waiting areas for drivers)

There, orders are assigned based on the arrival time of the driver. So we keep “a queue” of drivers in the system. If there are 3 drivers waiting, a newly created order will go to the first driver who arrived in the area.

In DISPATCH AREAS page we already have some “rejection thresholds” (see screen). When driver performs this number of actions, he will be put at the end of the queue. So if I am a driver and i reject rides with “Client Did Not Show” for 3 times, i will be put last in queue. 

This was done to mitigate bad driver behavior and cherry-picking of rides by them

!image-20241113-090853.png|width=620,height=386,alt="image-20241113-090853.png"!



This new “block feature” is an extension of the above. 

If drivers keep behaving bad (= rejecting rides) we will block them *from the area only* for X minutes. So:

* the block is caused by repetitive bad driver behavior
* the block is temporary and will last for X minutes as configured in the page
* driver will just need to wait until block expires. But of course they can keep getting rides regularly outside the dispatch-area in which they are blocked

* admin-panel UI is not deployed yet as we need to test it with QA but it will be available in DISPATCH-AREAS menu and will look like this.
!image-20241113-090644.png|width=799,height=386,alt="image-20241113-090644.png"!


Hope this clarifies a bit, let me know if you have further questions!

Hi team, 

This is not a bug, but a feature. 

The additional charges are related to incremental authorizations. 

Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change. 

The additionally authorized amounts have been released to the customer. 

Please note that we are not able to advise on why the payments were displayed to the customer a couple of days later. This can be specific to the customers bank and we cannot do anything about it. 

Cheers, 
Marten
